# Sample provenance

Only controlled captures and synthetic fixtures belong in this repository.
Do not add production dumps or logs, even after renaming their package prefixes.

- `thread-dumps/real-java-all-1-snapshot.txt` and
  `thread-dumps/real-java-all-3-snapshots.txt` were captured from the standalone
  scenario generator in `tools/thread-dump-generator`. The browser's built-in
  TDA sample is a copy of the three-snapshot capture. Its older
  `com.robbanhoglund.threaddump` frames are retained as originally captured;
  future captures use `com.robbanhoglund.jvmscope.samples.threaddump`.
- `frontend/test/tda/fixtures/class-initialization-vm-threads.txt` is entirely
  synthetic. It covers ten class-initialization waiters, one waiting initializer,
  and seventeen header-only VM threads. It replaces tests that previously
  depended on an operational dump.
- TDA fixtures under `frontend/test/tda/fixtures/` are synthetic unless their
  `runtime/` directory and the compatibility reports identify a controlled JVM
  capture. They include intentionally malformed and malicious text for parser
  and HTML safety tests.
- TLS runtime fixtures under `frontend/test/tls/fixtures/` were generated by
  `tools/tls-log-generator` against temporary loopback servers. JSSE debug output
  can include ephemeral test-session secrets. These are test captures, not
  credentials for an external system. No private keystore is committed.

The [public example library](../docs/EXAMPLES.md) explicitly selects controlled
runtime fixtures and labelled synthetic cases. It serves them as static files
without uploading user data. Dedicated synthetic teaching files live under
`frontend/assets/javautils/samples/`; the TLS files are regenerated with
`scripts/generate-tls-examples.mjs`. Malicious safety fixtures and unrelated
regression inputs are not part of this library.

`tda-cpu-hot-sequence.txt` and `tda-virtual-workers.json` in that teaching directory
are complete controlled Java 25 captures from `ThreadLibraryScenarios.java`.
The adjacent provenance JSON records the JDK, source hash, capture commands and
exact file hashes. They contain only the isolated example JVM's threads. Recreate
them with `scripts/capture-thread-examples.mjs`; their original JVM records are
not hand-written or edited. Only CPU line-ending normalization and actual
collector timestamps are added. See the example guide for the format limits.

The compatibility and deployment reports copied from the predecessor are marked
as historical. They do not assert that the renamed JvmScope build has already
been deployed. Current verification is recorded separately in the root README.
## Automated JVM evidence

`jvm-samples/` contains immutable reports and verified captures imported from
controlled JVM workloads. The importer checks hashes and replays the browser
parsers before writing. Ordinary tests replay them and verify generated README
and detailed results. Failed/raw captures are workflow artifacts, not fixtures.
Git preserves their bytes and excludes these captures from whitespace cleanup:
HotSpot/JSSE output can legitimately contain trailing whitespace and mixed line endings.
See [collection and import](../docs/JVM-SAMPLES.md).
